requirements.statement: When /audit-build closes a feature after a chained fix run that did not end STUCK, the custody anchor a first /ship-build sets is the branch head after that fix run committed, so the first custody check finds no changed shipped code and asks for no re-proof. Must pass.
The audit report and closed.json keep the commit the audit actually examined (auditedCommit) as its own truthful field, distinct from the anchor. Must pass.
A feature closed with no chained fix run, closed by the owner, or whose fix run ended STUCK, anchors exactly as today (the audited commit, else the pushed head).

closed.json's audit object gains anchorCommit: the full id of git rev-parse HEAD taken once the chained fix run is completely done (including its end-of-run whole-branch review and that review's edit commit), written only when this round chained a fix run, its RETURN line is not RETURN → STUCK, and decide returned close: true; otherwise null. If the review's [review-pending] row is still unresolved at close time, anchorCommit is null. auditedCommit stays the report header's value.

custody.js reconcile, when no anchor is set, prefers a valid audit.anchorCommit (anchor source 'audit-fixed'), then audit.auditedCommit (source 'audited'), then the head (source 'pushed'). A present but unresolvable anchorCommit is refused with a reason naming it, as an unresolvable auditedCommit is today.

Checkable outcome: with closed.json auditedCommit = A and anchorCommit = F, where F is A plus fix-run commits touching shipped source followed only by record-file commits, the first reconcile returns action 'set' with anchor F and a second reconcile returns action 'none'. With anchorCommit absent or null on the same history, the first reconcile anchors at A and does not return 'none' or 'set'. The test fails if the new field is ignored.

Non-goal, stated as a constraint: no change to check, move, affectedIds, the base excuse, path classes or re-proof rules; no change to /close-feature's owner close (audit: null) or to /task closes; no change to audit-rounds.js or what a re-audit reads.

tasks.description: custody.js reconcile: prefer closed.json audit.anchorCommit (source audit-fixed) over audit.auditedCommit when no anchor is set; refuse an unresolvable one; update the header comment and the vendored copy. Tests in packages/core/lib/custody.test.js (cases a, b, c: fix-run anchor set and re-reconcile none; null anchorCommit anchors at A; bad anchorCommit refused).

/audit-build close: once the chained fix run has returned and its end-of-run review result and edits are committed, record anchorCommit (post-fix git rev-parse HEAD) in closed.json's audit object only when this round chained a fix, its RETURN line is not STUCK, and decide returned close; otherwise null. auditedCommit stays the report header's value. Update docs/reference/other-commands.md closed.json row (anchorCommit nullable); sync the vendored command copy. New contract tests in packages/core/commands/verify-command-surface.test.js.

could_not_verify: A live /audit-build then /ship-build on github-live-test showing the first custody check asks for no re-proof: deferred by the plan; it waits on this build.

The wait for the fix run's background review is prose the model follows. If the model closes before the review returns, the rule degrades to anchorCommit null (today's behaviour), not to a wrong anchor, but that degradation is itself only checked by contract tests.
Whether the model running /audit-build reliably distinguishes a STUCK RETURN line from a successful one is prose-following, checked only by contract tests here.
